probes.mechanism: Internal model signals can trigger an interruption and hold tool calls until another reasoning model reviews the action.
probes.conditions: OpenAI describes deployment from GPT-5.6 onward, supervised labels and held-out tests. Internal activations must be accessible and the system must be able to intercept the relevant action before execution.
probes.counterexample: Unknown or untrainable behaviors remain outside the demonstrated scope. A classifier can trigger review without that review being correct, timely or able to stop every path.
probes.evidence: The developer reports greater resistance than text classifiers on tested attacks and transfer across many post-training stages. This is a November 2 methods report; experiment dates and individual model versions are unspecified.
probes.limits: Figures need not represent deployed classifiers; escalation is not the false-positive rate. New pretrained bases and drifting weights can require retraining. No operational harm-reduction rate or independent replication is established.
probes.mitigation: Record the measured defensive improvement while separately assessing coverage, adaptive attacks, reviewer judgment and blocking authority. Do not convert a reported deployment into validated protection against all failures.
probes.readerContext: Both languages explain internal signals as information calculated inside the AI, and state that another AI reviews the held operation. No assumption that a person provides the approval is introduced.
probes.whyHere: C3a concerns missed danger. This scoped addition complements the October monitoring evidence and leaves limited/tested classification and its October 28 full-review date unchanged.

recovery.mechanism: An agent can correct an intermediate mistake without completing the overall task; predicting recovery is a further, separate measurement.
recovery.conditions: 1,259 existing OSWorld/Web traces contain 1,403 annotated errors. Three researchers verify AI annotations. Desktop models are Claude 3.7 Sonnet, Sonnet 4.5 and Kimi K2.5; Web uses SeeAct with GPT-5-2025-08-07 on August 13, 2025.
recovery.counterexample: 725 errors recover, yet only 60% of 280 traces recovering all annotated errors finish their task. Remaining unannotated or later problems can still prevent completion.
recovery.evidence: Read the original version-1 methods, counts and task-disjoint prediction evaluation. ReCoF combines GLM-5.3-Flash assessments with frozen encoders and fusion; reported prediction improvement does not execute interventions.
recovery.limits: Observational associations do not isolate a causal effect of recovery. Older traces are not today’s capability ceiling or an ordinary-use incident sample. Researcher verification follows AI labels, and task-disjoint prediction is not evidence of beneficial human intervention.
recovery.mitigation: Use task completion, recovery and intervention outcomes as separate evaluations. Predictions can motivate a future intervention experiment but do not justify a proven policy of waiting or intervening.
recovery.readerContext: Japanese and English explain the difference between fixing a mistake and finishing work. Publication on October 27 is separated from the 2025 Web execution date.
recovery.whyHere: C2a is the relevant execution-capability condition. The study adds a limitation and an evaluation improvement without changing permissions, harmful intent or control-loss conditions.

treasury.mechanism: Finding a source, reading the correct digits and returning a reliable final answer are distinct parts of a document workflow.
treasury.conditions: 70 human-reviewed numeric questions over 1,435 scanned Treasury documents, ten model–harness pairs, three attempts per task and a 30-minute limit. Web search is disabled but a network-capable shell and Reducto reader are available.
treasury.counterexample: Opus 5.5/Claude Code succeeds on 64.8% of attempts but all three times on only 45.7% of tasks. Adjacent rankings are not significant after multiple-comparison correction; retrieval often succeeds where digit reading fails.
treasury.evidence: Read original sections 3–7, Table 2 and Appendix D. External-figure successes are reclassified as failures. Reader calls run October 3–21; October 28 is publication, while the underlying documents date from 1793–2024.
treasury.limits: Developer benchmark with mostly private tasks, pilot-driven wording/image adjustments, no human baseline and an unpinned reader. Model and harness effects are confounded. It does not test financial transactions, systemic finance or whole-job autonomy.
treasury.mitigation: Check figures against source images and measure repeatability and provenance. These are sensible verification requirements, not independently measured effects of a new defense in this paper.
treasury.readerContext: Both editions distinguish correct answers on individual attempts from stable success across repeated attempts and explain why financial source documents are not financial operations.
treasury.whyHere: Add to C2a, not to F4 or the systemic-finance branch. Preserve the distinction between a bounded workflow result and a complete causal path.

completion.mechanism: Completing a sequence requires the relevant skills, verification and recovery to transfer to the actual task; more general capability alone does not guarantee completion.
completion.conditions: Reread C2a and R0-C2a with METR’s human-time definition, Ironclad’s prepared contract tasks, low-resource-code evaluation, formalization and ReTerm. Parent C2 still requires C2a plus real-world access C2b.
completion.counterexample: Human-directed formalization, partial contract rubrics and language-specific tests can succeed while broader work still needs people. ReInBench and TreasuryQA provide additional failures of local success to imply reliable completion.
completion.evidence: Ironclad has 11 tasks and estimated rather than observed customer-time savings. ReTerm uses teacher-assisted, human-prepared recovery training; its non-tool error categories still recover at most 32%. Horizon measures human task time, not unattended model runtime.
completion.limits: Different metrics, models, harnesses and human roles cannot be pooled into a whole-job success rate. This review does not rerun experiments or infer the current ceiling from historical records.
completion.mitigation: Preserve bounded permissions, verification, exception handling and human escalation. Record recovery improvements alongside residual failures rather than treating every failed task as an absence of progress.
completion.readerContext: Read the actual Japanese and English C2a tour and detail text, parent C2, graph, current evidence and linked news. Explain task completion before connecting it to potential harm.
completion.whyHere: C2a was due November 3 and was substantively reread. Renew this node and its evidence clock only; R0-C2a retains its previous date. Keep limited/tested classifications and existing AND structure.

rsi.mechanism: Improved AI may help produce a subsequent useful improvement, creating feedback; a gain in one task or one cycle does not establish sustained whole-development acceleration.
rsi.conditions: Read MASS v1 methods and external evaluations, its public README, Phantom Gains v1, Anthropic’s RSI distinction, Amodei’s interpretation and the October GPT-6 card. Costs, human preparation, verification and transfer remain necessary conditions.
rsi.counterexample: MASS’s external Terminal-Bench and SWE-bench results decline. Phantom Gains obtains apparent improvements with unchanged-model controls. Neither result rules out all other feedback mechanisms.
rsi.evidence: MASS has two bounded cycles. Table 7 increases delivered outputs from 31/60 to 50/60 while the mean among delivered outputs falls from 3.07 to 2.88; unmatched subsets prevent a simple quality-decline inference. Public README still differs on task/trial counts.
rsi.limits: Paper 12 tasks times five trials differs from README 107 times three; held-out tasks can still enter workflow search. Per-output-token efficiency is not total compute, calendar time or human effort. No independently replicated unbounded RSI is inferred.
rsi.mitigation: Keep unchanged-model controls, external tasks and separate measures of output quality, delivery rate, total cost and human contribution. Do not treat developer risk thresholds as proof of no future RSI.
rsi.readerContext: The R3 tour and development-paths OR preserve progress without RSI and explain human-assisted versus fully autonomous feedback. R2 remains whole-process acceleration rather than code-volume growth.
rsi.whyHere: R3, R2-R3 and R3-R2 were due and are substantively renewed along with R3 evidence. Retain conditional forward connection, feedback return, limited/tested status and no automatic jump to ASI.

physical.mechanism: Physical task automation also needs reliable handling of exceptions, recovery and appropriate cost; selected robot-task success is not replacement of all physical work.
physical.conditions: Read Recova v1 physical tests and human roles, Anthropic’s job/evidence estimates and Gemini Robotics 2 selected-task demonstrations. Recova uses dual YAM arms, pi-0.5 task/recovery policies, a Gemini 3.8 Flash monitor and human-built digital twins/demos.
physical.counterexample: Human-corrected training raises the four-task average from 23.8% to 77.5%; adding recovery reaches 87.5%. The entire increase cannot be attributed to recovery. A separate 14-minute sequence still uses human control for 11% of the time.
physical.evidence: Four physical tasks have 20 trials per configuration. The final 0/7 human-intervention count is for one task/round. The robot-work estimate separates 34% technical feasibility in limited settings from 0.3% cost competitiveness.
physical.limits: Prepared tasks, demonstrations and unresolved human takeovers remain. A modeled work-exposure estimate is not observed job replacement. Selected whole-body demonstrations do not establish all-work coverage, affordability or adoption.
physical.mitigation: Evaluate exceptions, intervention burden and costs in the intended workplace. Preserve the technical-capability, deployment and distribution distinctions in the work route.
physical.readerContext: Read W2 in both tours and the W1-W4 joint connection. Both intellectual and physical work must cover the intended range, including exceptions, before the strong all-labor hypothesis can follow.
physical.whyHere: W2 was due and its limited/indirect classification is retained after substantive review. Renew W2 and its evidence date; W1-W4 keeps its existing date and joint conditions.

finance.mechanism: Financial disruption becomes systemic only if relevant AI use and propagation combine with inadequate buffers, timely stopping and recovery; the separate channels need not occur together.
finance.conditions: Reread F4 and joint F1-F3, the finance-conditions AND graph, current money summary and money story. Read the FSB final report sections 3.7/3.9 and BIS FSI analysis of response, recovery and dependencies.
finance.counterexample: Fallbacks, liquidity, loss absorption and recovery can limit a local problem. The Bank of Canada equity-tail analysis explicitly does not identify causal AI-adoption effects or operational transmission, so it is not evidence that F4 occurred.
finance.evidence: FSB recommends stopping, fallback, continuity and third-party planning; FSI discusses cyber resilience. These are original policy/analytical sources, not measured proof that defenses work or that all systemic conditions have been met.
finance.limits: Equity co-movement and frontier-AI cyber capability are not systemic financial failure. Historical/market proxies cannot supply missing permissions, exposure, propagation or failed-buffer conditions.
finance.mitigation: Keep fallback, independent recovery, provider diversification and stress-testing as conditional interventions. Do not convert recommended implementation into demonstrated reduction in crisis probability.
finance.readerContext: The money route separates earnings/profit, abundance and financial dysfunction. The TreasuryQA archive benchmark is deliberately not inserted as evidence of autonomous trading or system-wide harm.
finance.whyHere: F4 was due and remains a hypothesis after substantive rereading. Renew only the F4 node date; current money, F1-F3 and other clocks are preserved.

dependencies.mechanism: Capability, access, intent, missed danger, timely stopping, persistent loss of control and wider harm remain distinct conditions. Three additions do not establish that a complete pathway has occurred.
dependencies.conditions: Read changed bilingual passages and actual C2a/C3a/R3/W2/F4 tour stops, parents C2/C3/R2, four routes/stories, relevant graphs, current evidence and three linked news examples. Review the unchanged neighboring edge conditions.
dependencies.counterexample: A successful task can be benign or blocked by permissions; detecting danger may not stop it in time. Progress without RSI, physical exceptions and successful financial recovery preserve the alternative branches.
dependencies.evidence: Three primary-source/research pairs are added. Four due nodes and two due RSI edges are renewed; three matching evidence dates follow. C3a’s old date and all other clocks are preserved. All 41 edge IDs, topology and evidence classifications remain unchanged.
dependencies.limits: This is the November 3 daily and due-item review, not another complete Monday survey or independent replication. No date is advanced solely because an index was checked or a build passed. The current inventory is not a fresh audit of every historical source.
dependencies.mitigation: Include the tested defensive improvement, recovery gains and counterevidence. Keep intervention efficacy, deployment incidence and catastrophic outcomes separate; do not assign a new risk color or numerical extinction probability.
dependencies.readerContext: Both languages retain the same chronology, human roles, permissions and uncertainty. Local error recovery, scanned-document reading and internal monitoring are explained without requiring new glossary entries.
dependencies.whyHere: Map as-of, history, source inventory and translations must reflect the scoped addition. Dependency review validates the retained context without silently resetting its review dates.
